items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, main creamery 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: paid on butterfat by test, not weight; the station test governs (story 1).
Section A only calls Article VII 'the hinge of everything later'. The point that payment by weight would have cost nobody anything appears only in B3 and F, and credit does not travel into A.
Only Teague is named, with no 1905 start date. Effie Loomis as secretary/minute-book keeper and Hobart Sill as buttermaker are both absent.
Says Selby is Gideon's son but gives manager 'from 1911' (planted error; the key has 1913).
Story 5 (headed 1898-1925) describes the yearly 'station gain, five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account' line showing more fat received than credited.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, first-season glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Core mechanism given: weighed, sampled, tested in a bottle ruled for a full charge, cream hauled to Larrow Green, skim returned. 'Composite' is not said, but the item has no REQUIRED line.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice itemized: 6 dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Flat 0.19 every month, June flush and February alike, the mark of a proportional/instrument error (story 3).
Nothing says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that there was none in the county.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
No description of the test book's columns, the single hand, or the crossed-and-initialed corrections.
Gives 3.61 but not the summary leaf's recorded 1896 average of 3.80 on borrowed glass. Both figures are required; the run's 3.80 is the true average, not the 1896 leaf figure.

Nine weeks, 8 May-10 July 1911, borrowed measure, tests higher then back to the old level, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing (run says its sources lack it), but the item has no REQUIRED line and its core fact is present.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, largest patron; 'tested his own brother-in-law's milk'.
Has the 1919 circular but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why. Both bolded elements are required.
Died February 1934 after nine years under the charge; test book impounded 1925, to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book begun 1 January 1897, own scale against the station's, and the two agreed.
1902 complaints; gives 3.61 vs 3.78 and does not state the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19.
The committee came up in 'Grigg's sleigh' in January and reported in March, but the run never says it sampled January-March 1908 and does not name it as under Nyle Grigg.
200,000 lb at 3.42 in 1910; error called proportional, with Brant's gap of 0.18 'exactly 5%'.
Ivy borrowed the weigh book from Roy Brant in 1958; it went from Roy (d. 1962) to Hazel.
Jerome Cudd's factory at Alder Corners 'over the ridge', but Redlow Ridge and Vessey County (as its location) are not given, and both gate the point.
Four of the six Bottom farms hauled summer-flush milk over the ridge. 1915 is not given, but the core fact is there.
'Same cows and hay, different glass' at a different factory, i.e. other glassware plus other bench, framed as a control. Borderline.
The same milk tested 0.19 higher at Alder Corners. Sixteen seasons is not given (context only).
Uses the same-milk/different-building comparison to defeat the hay theory. Watering is not mentioned there, but that clause is unbolded.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, copied the Alder Corners figures for Ivy in 1958. 'Sixteen seasons' is not stated; core fact present.
Strawn described correctly, but Section A dates his lactometer visits 'from 1908' (NT-23 planted error; the key has 1907).
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, burette, whole lot condemned.
Strawn recorded the condemnation but 'nothing about what it had been doing for the twenty-six years before'.
Reorder 28 June and reply 2 July are right, but the 1924 average is given as 3.85 (planted error; the key has 3.80).
Crate to the station loft; notebooks to the state office on retirement, then the Farland library in 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Board sat 17 March-4 May 1925 in three sittings, two in the station weigh room. Frick is unnamed ('an Ashlin attorney'); the item has no REQUIRED line.
Three theories argued (water, tester skimming cream, wet hay); board found no cause established.
Four books listed including Strawn's condemnation-year notebook; nobody set it beside the others.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before any finding; award 4 May, $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
Gives one-fifth of $19,000 but never says the award was charged to the account into which the loss had accumulated as 'gain'.
Ivy b. 1931, granddaughter, graduate student in dairy husbandry at Farland under Leland Vaught.
Gathered records no one had put together: weigh book, Strawn notebook, Cudd figures.
February 1958 and the loft are right, but the count is left open ('nine or eleven ... cannot be settled'); nine is bolded.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against a 17.6 mark (95%); 0.88 c.c. short in story 2.
Recorded = 0.95 x true over 1897-1923; 3.61 against 3.80; 0.19 is 5% of about 3.8.
40,000,000 lb over 25 full years, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and the 76,000 lb identified with the ledger's station-gain line ('the missing butterfat, recorded in ink').
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; 33 years after the dismissal, 24 after his death.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son, via r18/r17/r21.
Second cousins, derived via first cousins Roy and Duncan.
Full vs half siblings cannot be settled (pre-1889 pages not kept). The run wrongly adds that half siblings would make them half second cousins, but that clause is unbolded.
Gideon Vose, father.
Gideon's Article VII turned the glass error into money; the son ran the father's system.
Headline verdict: 'the better evidence is that there was none'. It ranks the family denial over hearsay, and E1 #7 marks it 'Resolved'. That is an assertion, not a declared inability.
Treats a family member's denial as outranking the other side instead of noting that no document names or denies a link. Counts only one asserter.
$90 accepted: working shown, and the run says explicitly it uses the long-run 25c because it lacks the 1910 price.
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Abstains: the 1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable is the station's measuring glass (the broken measure); one thing changed.
Tester, herds, pasture, season, separator, scales, acid held constant.
The result is given only as 'rose markedly ... fell back'. No 3.80 during the interval and no 3.61 on return; the run says it has no figure.
Cause lies in the glass, not the man, cows or hay; limits: size of error, which item, whether the borrowed glass was accurate.
1911 interval (r22/r24), ledger surplus (r23), post-1923 rise (r22), Alder Corners (r17): three or more narrators.
Independence argued from separate records; reasons 1-3 hold without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper question the entries? No.'
Yes, he knew the tests ran low (1919 circular, complaints since 1902).
Only two of the five valid: signed the ledger line every year, and the 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911 (wrong); no watering argued at the hearing; no 'never names the glassware'.
A03 asserted: headline verdict 'he did not know why ... none that he suspected the glass'. No declared inability to settle it.

Weigh book 1900 vs 1897 (custody list); Keddie's start 1895 vs 1896 (the station opening); 1908 committee vs 1925 board as two bodies. Orra's 1868 was also resolved. Cap reached. The run got the circular-families row (eleven), the Selby Vose row, the 1924 average row and the Strawn row wrong.
NT-14 ($77.39 in r19 and r20's prose, broken by adding the line items) and NT-18 (great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by r18 and r22's correction). No other pair noticed as a pair.
A04: cannot be settled, works books burned in 1931. A06 (whose measure) not addressed. A10's undated by-laws appear only in Section A and are not framed as the 1891/92/93 conflict.
r20's 'nothing before 1900' against its own 1897 invoice; r18's 1868 against 'eighty-two in 1948'.

Pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, 0.19 = 5% of 3.80, onset 1 May 1897 on ending the borrowing, cessation June 1923, nothing else changed. The 1924 figure is given as 3.85 (deducted separately); the 1924 value is unbolded context.
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer, the ledger and Brant's agreeing scales.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus arriving heavy, the 1911 interval and the post-1923 rise under the same man.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 in winter, nothing in summer) and the Alder Corners book.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glass? No.'
A05 asserted: 'What did the tester believe? From 1911, the glass.'
About 138 words.
Invoice, weigh book, ledger, inspector's notebook, rival factory's tests, 1958 measurement.
No decoy stated as fact; headline numbers 3.61/3.80/76,000/$19,000/$3,800 all correct.
5% (one part in twenty), 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.
